source_text:
ταῦτα ἤδη γέγονε 86
καὶ ἀνταπόδοσις ἀξία ἐκληρώθη ἑκάστῳ, ἢ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως ἀνατυποῖ τὴν
εἰκόνα ἐν τούτοις; ἀλλά, φησίν, ὁπότε ὀνομάζει Λαζάρου προσηγορίαν, ἀληθῶς
γέγονε καὶ ἐπράχθη. διὰ τί γὰρ μὴ εἶπε Πτωχὸς δέ τις ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλὰ Λάζαρος; ἵνα
τῇ προσηγορίᾳ δείξῃ πείρᾳ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ ταῦτα πεπράχθαι. Ἐπίλυσις Τὴν κρίσιν κτλ.
Θʹ.
thought_title: Whether the Lazarus story already happened or images the coming judgment
orientation: An unnamed interlocutor raises the question whether the rich man and Lazarus account has already been enacted with due recompense, or whether it images the coming judgment, and argues from the naming of Lazarus that it truly happened.
pass_a_gloss: Have these things already happened, and was a worthy recompense allotted to each, or does he prefigure the coming judgment in these things? But, he says, whenever he names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted. For why did he not say 'some poor man,' but 'Lazarus'? In order that by the name he might show that these things actually happened. Solution: The judgment etc. 9.

choices.why: The verb ἀνατυπόω means to form or represent as an image; keeping the cognate object preserves the rhetorical force of the question.
The passive of κληρόω conveys the idea of receiving by lot or divine assignment, fitting the context of each person's due portion.
The dative pair contrasts actual experience with mere representation; 'experience' preserves πεῖρα's sense of real occurrence.
This is the heading introducing Cyril's own response; the glossary does not cover it, so a plain rendering is used.

bible_refs.note: ὀνομάζει Λαζάρου προσηγορίαν refers to the gospel naming of Lazarus; the interlocutor contrasts this with saying 'some poor man' (Πτωχὸς δέ τις ἄνθρωπος).

pass_b_english: Have these things already happened, and has each person been allotted the recompense he deserved? Or does he prefigure in them the coming judgment? But, the objector says, since Christ names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted. For why did Jesus not say, “Some poor man,” but “Lazarus”? So that by the name he might show that these things actually happened. Solution: the judgment, etc. Question 9.
notes: The numeral 86 after γέγονε appears to be a page or section number in the manuscript and is not part of the sentence.
The heading Ἐπίλυσις Τὴν κρίσιν κτλ. is lacunose; κτλ. indicates the text breaks off.

last_rejected.quote: does he image forth in them the image of the coming judgment
last_rejected.source_quote: ἢ τῆς μελλούσης κρίσεως ἀνατυποῖ τὴν εἰκόνα ἐν τούτοις
last_rejected.why: Subject is wrong: ἀνατυποῖ is 3rd singular, but 'he' implies Jesus/author; actually 'it' (the story/account) images forth.
last_rejected.fix: Or does it image forth in them the image of the coming judgment?
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνατυποῖ 3rd sg. subject is contextually understood; 'he' (Jesus/scripture) is reasonable, not a meaning-changing error.

last_rejected.quote: since he names the name of Lazarus
last_rejected.why: ὁπότε means 'when'/'since when'/'if', not causal 'since'; this changes the interlocutor's argumentative force.
last_rejected.fix: But, he says, when he names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁπότε with indicative commonly means 'when' or 'since'; causal 'since' is within normal range here.

problems.quote: image forth in them the image
problems.why: Intro says 'typifies' but text has convoluted 'image forth the image'

variants.text: image forth in them the image

problems.why: Three different phrases for same concept of literal occurrence

problems.quote: But, he says, since he names
problems.why: Unclear whether 'he says' refers to Jesus, the interlocutor, or an earlier authority

problems.quote: For why did he not say
problems.fix: Specify 'For why did Jesus not say'

problems.quote: does he image forth in them the image of the coming judgment
problems.fix: does he prefigure the coming judgment

problems.quote: Or does he image forth in them the image of the coming judgment?
problems.why: Awkward repetition of 'image' as verb and noun; unclear meaning.
problems.fix: Or does he present in them a figure of the coming judgment?

problems.quote: But, he says, since he names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted.
problems.why: Reader cannot tell who 'he says' refers to—the interlocutor or Christ.
problems.fix: But, the objector says, since Christ names Lazarus...

problems.quote: it truly happened and was enacted
problems.why: Both render the same concept of events occurring literally; different phrasing may confuse.
problems.fix: Use one consistent phrase for 'actually occurred.'

edits.old: Or does he image forth in them the image of the coming judgment?
edits.new: Or does he prefigure in them the coming judgment?

edits.old: But, he says, since he names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted.
edits.new: But, the objector says, since Christ names the name of Lazarus, it truly happened and was enacted.

edits.old: For why did he not say, “Some poor man,” but “Lazarus”?
edits.new: For why did Jesus not say, “Some poor man,” but “Lazarus”?

edits.old: So that by the name he might show that these things were enacted in experience and truth.
edits.new: So that by the name he might show that these things actually happened.

fixed: The English already says the same thing for the remaining problems; no further changes needed.
